content:
Apple is preparing to launch multiple new home products, but according to the latest report from Bloomberg, the company is simultaneously developing a home security and monitoring service, expected to debut in 2027.

Apple's home security and monitoring service is expected to launch in 2027, with the related information coming from Mark Gurman.

Apple is about to undergo a major revamp of its home product lineup, including an all-new Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini, and a home control hub (HomePad), with several new products expected to debut in the near future.

Mark Gurman has laid out Apple's product roadmap in detail in his latest report, noting that the company's home business ambitions also include a service.

When discussing products expected to launch in 2027, Gurman wrote:

The final sentence is key: "This new service will apply to a brand-new home security and monitoring service."

Gurman had previously hinted at Apple's intentions to enter the home security space, but now it appears the company really does plan to launch an actual service.

The home security and monitoring market is massive, with significant potential to boost the profitability of Apple's services business.

If Apple does indeed launch a paid home security and monitoring service, it may also be included in the Apple One bundle to boost appeal and retain more subscribers.

The emergence of this new service also seems to be a positive signal, showing that Apple is truly committed to taking the smart home space seriously. In other words, new products like this security sensor may only be the first step in expanding the product line.

Are you interested in using Apple's home security service? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
